$comment: Pathway definitions for the audience selector. Three pathways A/B/C aligned to L1/L2/L3 with cumulative semantics: B requires every L1 + L2 criterion in matrix.json; C requires every L1 + L2 + L3 criterion. Pathway C has six sub-domains; each sub-domain may add or relabel criteria scoped strictly to the Ethics dimension at L3 via 'ethics_overlay'. Other dimensions are constant across sub-domains.

pathways.name: Accessible
pathways.tagline: I want to publish this on Figshare, my institutional repository, GitHub, or as supplementary material to a paper.

pathways.name: Faithful
pathways.tagline: I want to publish this on Hugging Face, Kaggle, OpenML, or Dataverse — anywhere that expects ML-ready metadata.

pathways.name: Task-ready
pathways.tagline: I want this dataset to support model training in a regulated or sensitive domain — biomedical, clinical, or institutional human-subjects data.

sub_domains.name: General
sub_domains.description: Standard L3 ethics evidence as written in Table 11. Default datasheet template with an ethics-evidence section.

sub_domains.name: Clinical / health data
sub_domains.description: Healthsheet template; surfaces IRB protocol ID, HIPAA de-identification method, and DUA reference.

ethics_overlay.label: IRB protocol ID
ethics_overlay.remediation: The number assigned by your institution's IRB. Required so reviewers can verify the approval if needed.

ethics_overlay.label: HIPAA de-identification method (Safe Harbor or Expert Determination)
ethics_overlay.remediation: HIPAA recognises two methods. State which one applies; for Expert Determination, name the expert and the report date.

ethics_overlay.label: Data-use agreement template URL
ethics_overlay.remediation: PhysioNet, MIMIC, and CHoRUS provide template DUAs that can be reused.

sub_domains.name: Genomic / functional-genomics
sub_domains.description: Surfaces consent type, dbGaP accession, and re-identification risk assessment.

ethics_overlay.label: Consent type (general research use vs. disease-specific)
ethics_overlay.remediation: Genomic consent commonly distinguishes 'general research use' from 'disease-specific use'. Record the exact wording from the consent form.

ethics_overlay.label: dbGaP study accession (if applicable; mark N/A otherwise)
Re-identification risk assessment
ethics_overlay.remediation: Genomic data carries non-trivial re-identification risk even after standard de-identification. Document the method and threshold used.

sub_domains.name: Voice / public-health biomarker
sub_domains.description: Surfaces speaker consent, demographic representation audit, and accent / language coverage.

ethics_overlay.label: Speaker consent terms (collection, secondary use, voice-cloning restrictions)
ethics_overlay.remediation: Voice data implicates re-identification and impersonation risks; consent must explicitly cover or exclude voice cloning and biometric uses.

ethics_overlay.label: Demographic representation audit across speakers
ethics_overlay.remediation: Counts and proportions across age, sex, race/ethnicity, and primary language.

ethics_overlay.label: Accent and language coverage statement
ethics_overlay.remediation: Document the accents and languages represented and any that are absent. Coverage gaps constrain valid downstream uses.

sub_domains.name: Salutogenesis / multi-modal precision health
sub_domains.description: Surfaces multi-modal alignment provenance, longitudinal consent, and modality-specific de-identification.

ethics_overlay.label: Multi-modal alignment provenance (how participant identities are linked across modalities)
ethics_overlay.remediation: Linking labs to imaging to wearables produces re-identification surface area beyond any single modality. Document the linkage method and the identifier used.

ethics_overlay.label: Longitudinal consent terms (re-contact, withdrawal, data retention)
ethics_overlay.remediation: State whether participants may withdraw, what happens to already-collected data, and how re-contact is governed.

ethics_overlay.label: Modality-specific de-identification methods (imaging, wearable, lab)
ethics_overlay.remediation: Each modality has its own de-identification standards (DICOM tag stripping for imaging, accelerometer windowing for wearables). Document each.

sub_domains.name: Institutional / human-subjects (non-clinical)
sub_domains.description: Surfaces IRB or equivalent committee approval and tiered-access policy. Targets institutional Dataverse with restricted-access tier and ICPSR for social-science data.

ethics_overlay.label: Reviewing body (IRB, ethics committee, or equivalent)
ethics_overlay.remediation: Name the institution and the committee. Required so reviewers can verify the review record if needed.

ethics_overlay.label: Tiered-access policy URL
ethics_overlay.remediation: Institutional Dataverse and ICPSR both publish tiered-access policies; link to the one that applies.
